items.title: Mother, child get 2-day remand as police probe stray dog operation assault
items.summary: MUAR: Police have opened two investigation papers into a mother and her child over the assault of a Muar Municipal Council (MPM) enforcement officer during an operation to catch stray dogs. The incident allegedly occurred here at Taman Bintang Emas, Bukit Pasir, two days ago. "Investigations found that the incident occurred at about 5.45am two days ago while MPM enforcement officers were conducting an integrated operation to catch stray dogs in the area.

items.title: Anwar calls for pondok schools to be upgraded to university level
items.summary: PASIR MAS: Pondok institutions should be strengthened and upgraded to university level to ensure they remain relevant to the changing needs of society. He said pondok institutions had long served as a stronghold for the Muslim community, particularly in protecting its faith, moral values and knowledge. Anwar said Islamic educational institutions must adapt to changing circumstances while continuing to uphold the principles and guidance of Islamic scholars.

items.title: 181 undocumented migrants arrested in Chow Kit raid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 181 undocumented migrants were arrested during an Immigration Department raid at Pasar Raja Bot, Chow Kit. Immigration Department deputy director-general (Operations) Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli said 512 people were checked during Ops Mega Bersepadu. The others comprised 20 Bangladeshi men, three Indian men, five Nepali men, one Pakistani man and five people of other nationalities, including a child.

items.title: Police officer held over RM3,000 bribe to settle family fight case
items.summary: SEREMBAN: A police officer was arrested for allegedly taking a RM3,000 bribe from a couple to drop action over a fight involving their family member. The source said the bribe was sought as an inducement to refrain from taking action over the matter. "It was in exchange for not taking action over a fight involving a family member of a couple," the source said today.

items.title: PM recalls late pondok founder's advice, encouragement
items.summary: PASIR MAS: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was visibly moved as he recalled his close relationship with the late founder of Madrasah Ar-Rahmaniah Ad-Diniah, Abdullah Abdul Rahman, during a gathering with about 200 congregants tonight. Anwar spent more than 10 minutes sharing his personal experiences and memories of the late religious scholar, whom he said had played an important role in encouraging and strengthening his resolve more than 20 years ago. Anwar said he was deeply touched by his visit to the religious institution today as he continued to hold the late Abdullah in high regard and had always prayed for him.

items.title: [UPDATED] Sultan of Selangor contracts Influenza A, state ceremony postponed
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah is unwell after contracting Influenza A, the Selangor Royal Office said today. In a statement, Istana Alam Shah said the infection was confirmed by his personal physicians, Datuk Dr Anuar Onah and Datuk Dr Tan Hui Meng. "Alhamdulillah, His Highness's health is gradually improving, although he is still experiencing a fever," the statement said tonight.

items.title: Anwar announces RM200mil increase in business grants under Skim Usahawan Bangkit
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The Federal Government will increase grants under the Skim Usahawan Bangkit by RM200 million next year to help small entrepreneurs expand their businesses and boost their earnings. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said even modest allocations could make a significant difference when channelled directly to businesses in need. He said relatively small purchases, such as affordable refrigerators to preserve stock, could prevent losses and generate thousands of ringgit in additional monthly income.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Saturday, Oct 31, 2026

items.title: Fahmi extends condolences over death of Mata Ayer assemblyman
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has expressed his condolences to the family of Mata Ayer assemblyman Wan Badariah Wan Saad, who died today. Wan Badariah died at Tuanku Fauziah Hospital in Kangar at 4.26pm. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Fahmi offers condolences to family of Mata Ayer state assemblyman Wan Badariah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has expressed his condolences to the family of Mata Ayer State Assemblyman Wan Badariah Wan Saad, who passed away today. Fahmi also prayed that Allah SWT would forgive the deceased’s sins, bless her soul, and place her among the believers and the righteous. Wan Badariah passed away at Tuanku Fauziah Hospital in Kangar at 4.26pm.

items.title: Anwar directs Education Ministry to act firmly on school bullying
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the Ministry of Education (MOE) to take firm action against bullying in schools amid growing concerns over children’s safety and well-being. He said cases involving children, including suicide, abuse and bullying, highlighted the need to strengthen character development and moral values from an early age. Anwar said academic excellence alone was insufficient, stressing that education must also instil good manners, respect and a sense of responsibility among students.

items.title: Anwar, Lawrence Wong to witness JS-SEZ master plan launch; Perak venue under review, says Akmal Nasrullah
items.summary: Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said it had been agreed that the launch would be witnessed jointly by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Singaporean counterpart, Lawrence Wong. “Both prime ministers have agreed to witness the launch of the master plan. On preparations for Monday’s bilateral meeting in Singapore, Akmal Nasrullah said Singapore would host the meeting.

items.title: Chicken killed by electric current may have reached Muslim eateries
items.summary: Selangor Islamic Religious Council (Mais) chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin said preliminary investigations found that the premises used the water-bath stunning method, with excessively high electric voltage believed to have caused the chickens to die before slaughter. He said the council was concerned that the chicken supply had reached Muslim-owned restaurants. he said.

items.title: National Courier Day: Govt pledges reform as RM6.9b courier sector takes spotlight
items.summary: MCMC said the government remains committed to strengthening the postal and courier industry through regulatory reform, strategic cooperation and digital transformation to improve service efficiency, industry competitiveness and consumer safety. “On regulatory reform, the government is reviewing proposed amendments to the Postal Services Act 2012 (Act 741) and plans to gazette the Postal Services Regulations (Postal Service Security and Prohibited Postal Articles) 2026 (PSR2026), subject to the relevant approval process. Also present were Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah, MCMC managing director Abdul Karim Fakir Ali, AMEC chairman Ronald Tan, and representatives of government agencies, postal and courier industry players.

items.title: BN to focus on candidates, policies in Melaka election
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional will not resort to smear campaigns in the Melaka election, focusing instead on its candidates, service records, manifesto pledges and solutions for voters. Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said voters should assess candidates based on their capabilities, experience and plans to take the state forward. Azalina said candidates, party workers and supporters should campaign fairly, comply with election rules and avoid provocations involving race, religion and royalty.

items.title: Nga Kor Ming urges global cooperation on housing crisis, cites 3.4 billion affected
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Stronger international cooperation is needed to address the global housing crisis, with approximately 3.4 billion people worldwide experiencing some form of inadequate housing, said Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. The event, themed “Regenerating the City: Adequate Housing for All”, is jointly organised by UN-Habitat, China’s Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, the Fujian Provincial People’s Government and the Fuzhou Municipal People’s Government. He highlighted the Malaysia Madani vision, the country’s housing reform agenda, and the National Housing Policy 2026-2035 as key initiatives to improve housing accessibility and support sustainable urban development.

items.title: KL police arrest 18 Taiwanese for posing as Hong Kong police in online scam
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Police detained 18 Taiwanese nationals suspected of involvement in an online scam syndicate impersonating Hong Kong police after raids on two luxury apartment units here on Thursday. Dang Wangi police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said 17 men and one woman, aged between 19 and 43, were arrested during the 6.35pm raid. “Police seized 69 mobile phones, five laptops, and two sets of Hong Kong police uniforms,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Anwar contributes RM200,000 to madrasah in Pondok Lubuk Tapah for repairs
items.summary: PASIR MAS, Oct 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today presented a contribution of RM200,000 to Madrasah Ar-Rahmaniah Ad-Diniah Pondok Lubuk Tapah here. Also present were Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud and Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat. Madrasah Ar-Rahmaniah Ad-Diniah Pondok Lubuk Tapah was founded in 1931.

items.title: Anwar allocates RM200,000 for madrasah restoration
items.summary: PASIR MAS: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today handed over a RM200,000 mock cheque for the maintenance and restoration of Madrasah Ar-Rahmaniah Ad-Diniah at Pondok Lubuk Tapah here. The allocation was part of the 2026 Maintenance and Restoration Project for Islamic Educational Institutions in Kelantan. The mock cheque was received by the madrasah's chairman, Datuk Dr Luqman Abdullah.

items.title: UK PM 'open' to slavery apology but not reparations
items.summary: LONDON: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Saturday he was "open" to the UK issuing a formal apology for its role in the transatlantic slave trade, but ruled out financial reparations. The Labour leader made the remarks days before attending a Commonwealth leaders summit in Antigua and Barbuda, as King Charles III tours the Caribbean. The transatlantic slave trade was a "brutal and barbaric violation" of the rights of those enslaved, he said.

items.title: 17 held after reported fight at Ampang flat
items.summary: AMPANG: Police have detained 17 people to assist in investigations into a reported fight at Flat Lembah Jaya. Ampang Jaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid said a patrol car unit was dispatched to the scene after receiving an emergency call at 2.07am. "Seventeen people were detained to assist in investigations under Section 148 of the Penal Code.

items.title: 2 women held after Muar dog-catching operation
items.summary: MUAR: Two women have been arrested following an incident involving a Muar Municipal Council enforcement officer during a stray dog-catching operation in a residential area yesterday. Muar district police chief Assistant Commissioner Raiz Mukhliz Azman Aziz confirmed that police had received a report on the case and said the two women were arrested to assist in investigations. The officer subsequently lodged a police report.

items.title: RM16b in SARA, STR aid for Malaysians as helping the poor won’t bankrupt the govt, says Anwar
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — The government will not become poor or go bankrupt by helping the less fortunate, as the real threats to the country’s economy are misconduct among leaders, corruption and financial leakages, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said providing assistance to low-income groups was the government’s responsibility to ensure that the benefits of national development were shared more widely among the people. “No country or government has ever become poor simply by helping the poor,” he said when launching the Kelantan Entrepreneur Revival Scheme here today.

items.title: Jom Heboh carnival draws bigger crowds on second day
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: The second day of the Jom Heboh Carnival (KHJ) Johor Baru 2026 at Angsana Johor Baru Mall here continued to draw large crowds today. Residents from Johor and neighbouring Singapore took advantage of the weekend to visit the event. "My children love coming to the carnival.

items.title: Anwar unveils additional RM200m grant to support low-income, small-scale entrepreneurs
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — The government has allocated an additional grant of about RM200 million to strengthen the capacity of small-scale entrepreneurs, particularly those from low-income groups, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said small-scale financial assistance could generate meaningful returns for traders if channelled to meet their specific business requirements. On the Kelantan Usahawan Bangkit Scheme, Anwar said more than 4,000 applications had been received from B40 entrepreneurs, with 446 approved so far.

items.title: Anwar: Golok River mouth widening project to cut flood risk, talks with Thailand to wrap up within a month
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Oct 31 — Malaysia and Thailand are expected to finalise negotiations on the Golok River mouth widening project within a month to reduce flood risks in Kelantan and southern Thailand. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he had held two rounds of talks with the Thai government, including with his counterpart Anutin Charnvirakul, to expedite the implementation of the project. Also present was Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud.

items.title: 18 Taiwanese held in Kuala Lumpur scam syndicate raid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have dismantled an international call centre syndicate that used Kuala Lumpur as a base to scam victims overseas. "Police also seized 69 mobile phones, five laptops and two Hong Kong police uniforms. Based on the items recovered, the syndicate is suspected of carrying out scams by impersonating Hong Kong police officers and targeting victims in Hong Kong," he said.

items.title: Kimono-clad pets blessed at Japan festival lacking enough kids
items.summary: TOKYO: Chanting and swishing a wooden wand, a Japanese priest blessed a cat, a shiba inu and several Yorkshire terriers at a shrine in Tokyo on Saturday, in a rite usually reserved for children. The 46-year-old doctor said she had spent two months hand-crafting a bespoke, bright-red kimono for her cat, a five-year-old British shorthair called Amber. "This little one is like my child," she said.

items.title: All relief centres closed in Kedah, Negeri Sembilan as floods subside, Perak evacuees fall to 25
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Floods in Kedah and Negeri Sembilan have fully subsided, with all three temporary relief centres (PPS) in the two states closed today, while the number of evacuees in Perak has declined. In Kedah, the last relief centre in Pendang, Dewan Pejabat Penghulu Mukim Bukit Raya, which had been open since last Wednesday, was closed at 10am, allowing all nine evacuees from two families to return home after the floodwaters receded completely. In Negeri Sembilan, two relief centres in Kuala Pilah, Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Undang Johol and Dewan Orang Ramai Dangi, which housed 87 evacuees from 35 families, were also closed at 4pm today following improved weather and the complete recession of floodwaters.

items.title: Malaysia, Thailand to finalise Sungai Golok project to solve Kelantan, southern Thailand floods
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Malaysia and Thailand are expected to finalise negotiations on the Sungai Golok estuary project within a month to help mitigate flooding in Kelantan and southern Thailand. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he had had two rounds of discussions with the Thai government, including with its new prime minister, to expedite efforts to resolve the issue. "I have had discussions twice with Thailand, including with its new prime minister, to expedite the matter.

items.title: PWD assistance gets largest share of Women's Ministry's 2027 budget
items.summary: KUCHING: Assistance for people with disabilities (PWD) has received the largest allocation under the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry's 2027 Budget. Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said RM1.5 billion of the RM3.3 billion allocated to the ministry would go towards assistance for PWD, benefiting more than 300,000 recipients. She said the government had also allocated RM1.3 billion for elderly assistance and the care sector, which was expected to benefit nearly 200,000 recipients.

items.title: No unhealthy readings: Cheras highest at 77 as 47 areas nationwide record moderate API readings this afternoon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — A total of 47 areas across the country recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at a moderate level as of this evening, while 21 areas recorded good air quality. In Sarawak, seven areas recorded moderate readings: Mukah (64), IPD Serian (59), Kuching (57), Samalaju (56), Sri Aman (55), Sibu (53), and Samarahan (51). Kedah also recorded moderate readings in Sungai Petani (58) and Kulim Hi-Tech (51), while Kuala Terengganu in Terengganu recorded a reading of 55, and Labuan recorded 52.

items.title: Anwar says helping underprivileged will not impoverish country
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said helping the underprivileged would not impoverish the country, but misconduct and poor governance could weaken and destroy it. Anwar said cost-of-living assistance allocated this year amounted to RM16 billion, but the commitments would not burden the country. Anwar said the government would continue approving the remaining applications, noting that most applicants were women.

items.title: Mata Ayer assemblyman Wan Badariah dies at 50
items.summary: KANGAR: Mata Ayer assemblyman Wan Badariah Wan Saad has died. He said Wan Badariah died at Tuanku Fauziah Hospital at 4.26pm. Under the previous state administration, Wan Badariah served as state tourism committee chairman.

items.title: Perlis PAS announces death of Mata Ayer rep Wan Badariah
items.summary: KANGAR, Oct 31 — Mata Ayer assemblywoman Wan Badariah Wan Saad died at Hospital Tuanku Fauziah (HTF) here at 4.26pm today. Perlis PAS Information chief Mohamad Zahid Ibrahim announced her death in a post on the Perlis PAS Facebook page. He also extended condolences to her family and urged the public to pray for her soul.

items.title: Pregnant mother hides behind counter as sword-wielding robber strikes jewellery shop
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: A pregnant mother of three hid behind a counter in fear as a sword-wielding robber struck a jewellery shop in Damansara Damai yesterday. "It was only after the man had left that I heard the jewellery shop workers screaming 'robber, robber,' she said when met at the scene today. Yani said it all happened within minutes.

items.title: Baby buried in Kapit still hospitalised; mother’s postpartum depression link unconfirmed, says Nancy Shukri
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 31 — The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry (KPWKM) has yet to receive medical confirmation on whether the mother of a baby boy found buried in Kapit recently was suffering from postpartum depression. Its Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said registered counsellors and hospital medical personnel had important roles to play in identifying the underlying issues faced by the mother. Nancy said discussions on whether the baby would be placed under the care of family members or other suitable parties had yet to be concluded, as both the mother and baby were understood to still be receiving hospital treatment.

items.title: Anwar says technology must go hand in hand with good values
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Parents must instil good values and moral character in their children as the country advances in technology and artificial intelligence. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he would continue educating and reminding parents of their responsibility, stressing that national development must also be rooted in religious values, good manners and moral principles. Anwar said that while much attention was being given to entrepreneurship and economic development, equal emphasis must be placed on nurturing good character and moral values among the younger generation.

items.title: Sabah MMA seeks urgent deployment of doctors
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) has called on the Health Ministry to deploy more doctors from Peninsular Malaysia to critically understaffed healthcare facilities across Sabah. He said 11 of Hospital Ranau's 19 medical officers had been transferred out following the recent permanent appointment exercise. Brandon said the state health department's efforts to deploy three additional medical officers to Ranau in stages were constrained by similar shortages at other facilities across Sabah.

items.title: Not compulsory, but journalists, your annual check-up could soon come with your press card
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 31 — The Malaysian Media Council (MMC) should explore mechanisms to encourage media practitioners to undergo health screenings during the process of issuing media passes. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the proposed initiative is crucial to ensure that as many as possible of the 12,000 personnel in the media sector benefit and have health issues identified at an early stage. Also present were Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) Chief Executive Officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin, CVSKL Foundation chairman Tan Sri Rashpal Singh, ECM Libra Foundation chairman Datuk Seri Kalimullah Masheerul Hassan and MMC chairman Tan Sri Nallini Pathmanathan.

items.title: NSTP attracts visitors with subscription promotions, exclusive merchandise
items.summary: Visitors were also offered exclusive merchandise as part of the promotions. Visitors were introduced to NSTP's publications and subscription packages, including a complimentary one-year e-paper subscription promotion. The booth also featured New Straits Times-branded merchandise, including T-shirts, tote bags and umbrellas, as part of efforts to engage readers and promote the company's publications.

items.title: ‘Boss’ texts, RM486,000 gone: Johor Bahru woman duped by fake employer
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 31 — A woman fell victim to a scam after being deceived by an individual who impersonated her employer, resulting in the transfer of RM486,000 from the company. Acting Johor Bahru Utara district police chief Supt Azrol Anuar Nor said the 35-year-old victim was deceived through a short message service (SMS) from the individual who impersonated her company manager in the incident at 10 am. SMS stands for Short Message Service.

items.title: Puchong chicken supplier shut for two weeks after halal breach discovery, restaurants told to stop buying from it
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 31 — A premises in Puchong, suspected of slaughtering, processing and distributing chicken without valid halal certification, was found to be using the electric water-bath stunning method. Selangor Islamic Religious Council (Mais) chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin said preliminary inspections found that the electrical voltage used was believed to be too high, causing the chickens to die instantly before undergoing slaughter in accordance with Islamic law. “Early this morning, the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais), in collaboration with the police, the Selangor Department of Environment (DOE), the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) and the Petaling District Health Office, led a raid on premises allegedly involved in slaughtering chickens in a manner that did not comply with Islamic requirements.

items.title: Teen held for throwing stone at KTMB train
items.summary: ARAU: A 14-year-old boy was detained after throwing a stone at a Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) train, shattering a carriage window and injuring a passenger. Arau police chief Superintendent Ahmad Mohsin Md Rodi said the teenager was detained at a house in Kampung Guar Sanji today. "The boy admitted deliberately throwing a stone at the train window.

items.title: Ramanan, Fadhlina confident economic strength, political stability will give PH an edge
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Pakatan Harapan (PH) is confident that the country's improving economic conditions and current political stability could give the coalition an advantage in the 16th Melaka state election on Nov 14. Speaking to the media at the Machap Jaya Nomination Centre at the JAPERUN Machap Jaya Complex in Bukit Bulat today, he said the election outcome remained open and would depend on the people's acceptance of the respective coalitions' proposals and efforts. Meanwhile, PKR Wanita chief Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said PH's candidate for Machap Jaya, Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin of PKR, had extensive political experience and was no stranger to voters in Melaka.

items.title: Employee transfers RM486,000 company money, deceived by individual impersonating employer
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A woman fell victim to a scam after being deceived by a person who impersonated her employer, resulting in the transfer of RM486,000 from the company. Acting Johor Baru Utara district police chief superintendent Azrol Anuar Nor said the 35-year-old victim was deceived through a short message service (SMS) from the individual who impersonated her company manager in the incident at 10am. He said the victim was instructed to transfer the company's money to the suspect's account under the pretext of payment of a new contract.

items.title: Sabah is short of nearly 245 medical officers, and Ranau Hospital feels it most
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 31 — Sabah is facing a shortage of nearly 245 medical officers following the implementation of the Phase 2 Permanent Appointment exercise on September 28, with Ranau Hospital among the healthcare facilities affected by the transfer of existing medical officers. Ranau Hospital is currently operating with only nine medical officers, including the hospital director, after 11 of its 19 medical officers were transferred out under the exercise. It said the situation at Ranau Hospital reflected a broader shortage of medical officers across Sabah, with several other healthcare facilities facing similar challenges.

items.title: AGC reviewing candidate selection for proposed separation of top legal roles
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) is reviewing provisions on the selection of candidates under a proposal to separate the roles of the attorney-general and public prosecutor. Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said this followed the tabling of the Bill on the proposed separation. "The Bill on the proposed separation of the roles of attorney-general and public prosecutor has been tabled and has gone through the proper process, including consideration by the Parliamentary Special Select Committee (PSSC).

items.title: Three or four checks, then one big raid: How a Puchong chicken warehouse that flouted halal rules ran for 20 years
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — A chicken slaughtering and processing warehouse in Puchong, raided under Ops Taring Chiller yesterday, is believed to have operated for 20 years. Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Intelligence and Investigation (WCB/PSK) commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said investigations identified the warehouse owner as a 34-year-old local man. “Check results showed this fresh chicken slaughtering and processing warehouse has operated for roughly 20 years.

items.title: Too soon to count? PSD hasn’t measured Waze ban compliance yet
items.summary: KAMPAR, Oct 31 — The Public Service Department (JPA) is confident that civil servants will fully comply with the ban on the use of the Waze navigation application. Director-General of Public Service (KPPA) Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said the compliance rate among civil servants had yet to be determined, as the government had only recently announced the directive. Meanwhile, Wan Ahmad Dahlan said RM1.465 million had been allocated to improve infrastructure, upgrade public facilities and support educational programmes under the Kampung dan Sekolah Angkat Madani programme for residents of Kampung Kota Bharu and students of Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Malim Nawar here.

items.title: Amanah vs Umno in Merlimau: Rahayu knows Dr Akmal is big on social media, so she’s counting on voters at the grassroots
items.summary: JASIN, Oct 31 — A father’s advice to always remain strong and broad-minded has inspired Melaka Amanah Wanita chief Rahayu Hamzah to take on the challenge of contesting the Merlimau state seat for Pakatan Harapan (PH) in the 16th Melaka state election. She said the advice had become her guiding principle, particularly as she prepares to face Barisan Nasional (BN) incumbent Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh. Acknowledging Dr Muhamad Akmal’s strong social media influence as Umno Youth chief, Rahayu said she remained confident of PH’s support among voters in the constituency.

items.title: No five- or six-cornered fights in 28 seats: Melaka’s 2026 ballot looks very different from 2021
items.summary: Among the straight fights attracting attention is Tanjung Bidara, where incumbent Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh of Barisan Nasional (BN) faces Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate Mohd Yunazri Mustamiri, who is making his electoral debut. Duyong will see a straight fight between incumbent Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem of BN and PH candidate Poo Long Suan, a member of the DAP Melaka Complaints Committee. In Merlimau, incumbent Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh of BN will be challenged by PH candidate Rahayu Hamzah.

items.title: Child, 10, among 181 detained in Chow Kit immigration raid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — The Immigration Department detained 181 foreign nationals for various immigration offences during an integrated operation at Jalan Raja Bot, or Chow Kit Market, here this morning. Immigration Department deputy director-general (Operations) Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli said the operation began at 9.40 am and involved checks on 512 foreign nationals. “A total of 181 foreign nationals were detained for various immigration offences, including lacking valid travel documents, overstaying, and pass misuse,” he told reporters at the scene today.

items.title: Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir: MCA takes on DAP’s home turf
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 31 — Two additional state assembly seats to be contested by MCA candidates in the 16th Melaka state election, namely Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir, pose a significant challenge for the party to secure the people’s mandate in the state, especially from the Chinese community. He said the MCA always pays attention to the people of Melaka, including all the state assembly constituencies under the Kota Melaka parliamentary constituency, even though the area is a stronghold of the DAP. For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/.

items.title: Brothers on opposite sides: Akmal Salleh's sibling stands for Bersama in Melaka polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Dr Muhammad Solehin Saleh, the elder brother of Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh, is among 16 Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) candidates contesting the Melaka state election. Muhammad Solehin, 40, is representing the party in the Bemban state seat under the Jasin parliamentary constituency in a four-cornered fight, Sinar Harian reported. In the 2021 Melaka state election, Akmal retained the seat for Umno-BN with a majority of 3,248 votes.

items.title: Pakatan has both ends of the age scale covered: A 24-year-old law grad and a retired captain, 66
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — The youngest candidate in the 16th Melaka state election, Muhammad Mukhlisul Mubin Julasapiyah, will contest the Kuala Linggi state seat. Meanwhile, Capt (Rtd) Mohamad Jaafar, 66, also representing PH, is the oldest candidate in this election, contesting the Telok Mas seat against incumbent Datuk Abdul Razak Abdul Rahman of BN and Muhammad Hazwan Mustafa of Bersama. Telok Mas is one of five state seats under the Kota Melaka parliamentary constituency, with 29,751 eligible registered voters.

items.title: Stolen Hilux leads cops to syndicate behind eight 4x4 thefts in Perak and KL
items.summary: SITIAWAN, Oct 31 — Police have crippled a syndicate believed to be involved in stealing four-wheel-drive vehicles in Perak and Kuala Lumpur with the arrest of three people in Kampung Koh here on Tuesday. Manjung district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hasbullah Abd Rahman said the arrests were made following information and intelligence gathered after a report on the theft of a Toyota Hilux in Taman Mas 2, Sitiawan, on Oct 26. He said the Manjung district police headquarters received the report at about 10.06am that day.

items.title: Among the youngest in the race, Pakatan’s Nana says Kelebang needs a voice for women and young people
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 31 — Undeterred by her defeat in her first electoral contest in Sungai Rambai, Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir is once again throwing her hat into the ring in the 16th Melaka state election. The 26-year-old Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate, affectionately known as Nana, said her unsuccessful electoral debut at 21 had been a valuable learning experience, giving her renewed confidence to contest the Kelebang state seat. Meanwhile, Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate Datuk Lim Ban Hong said he was taking nothing for granted in the state election despite being the incumbent Kelebang assemblyman.

items.title: Police arrest 16 foreigners in raid on Jalan Ampang hotel penthouse ‘mini casino’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 31 — Police have detained 16 foreign nationals after raiding a hotel penthouse on Jalan Ampang where a “mini casino” was operating. Kuala Lumpur police chief Fadil Marsus said the raid was carried out at 1.50am today, according to a Free Malaysia Today report. “An investigation found that the penthouse was being used as a mini casino open only to close acquaintances, involving Chinese nationals only,” he said in a statement.

items.title: Same fix as 2023, please: Indian civil servants ask Putrajaya to add Nov 10 as extra Deepavali day
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 31 — The Putrajaya Indian Civil Servants Association (Imaiyam) is appealing to the government to grant unrecorded leave (CTR) to Hindu civil servants on Tuesday, November 10, as this year’s Deepavali leave overlaps with a public holiday and its replacement holiday. Imaiyam chairman Dr Sathiskumar K. Muthusamy said the request is not aimed at securing a new benefit, but at ensuring that the existing Deepavali CTR, long provided by the government, can be fully enjoyed by Hindu civil servants. As a result, the day usually used for CTR overlaps with the public holiday, and the benefit cannot be enjoyed,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
